about: Hand-written ground truth for retrieval over a whole class rather than one document.
Thirty-six documents of a real signals-and-systems course - eight problem sets, their
eight answer keys, four slide decks, five labs, two exams with solutions, a scanned
appendix, and a linear algebra textbook the course leans on - all in one class, which
is the search space the product actually has.
Every question names the document its answer is in with expect_document, and a chunk
from the right pages of the wrong document is scored as a miss. That is the whole point
of the set. A single-document workspace cannot tell a good answer from the only answer
available, and this course is full of documents that say nearly the same words: a
problem set and its answer key restate each question verbatim, the low-pass lab and the
high-pass lab are the same handout with one word changed, and the practice midterm and
its solution share an instructions paragraph character for character.
Pages were read before the questions were written. Where a fact appears on a run of
pages the range covers the run; where it appears once the range is that one page twice.
Two questions - mixed-signal-representations and dtft-to-dtfs - are asked of a slide
deck whose text layer extracts as scattered characters with the equations broken apart.
They are here deliberately. A course contains documents like that, and retrieval either
reaches them or it does not.
The controls name subjects no document in this class covers. Note that a control is a
weaker instrument here than in a one-book workspace: a class of thirty-six documents
can plausibly answer far more than one book can, so a control only rules out what the
whole course is silent about.

questions.question: What is the Fourier transform of e^{-4|t|}, worked out step by step?
questions.note: homework_5 poses this exact signal in the same notation and has no answer in it.

questions.question: Which signals does Homework Assignment 5 ask me to compute X(jw) for?
questions.note: The mirror of the question above. The answer key restates every one of them.

questions.question: How is the equivalent impulse response of the cascade of h1, h2 and h3 worked out when x(t) = e^{-t}u(t)?
questions.note: homework_3 poses the same cascade in the same notation and works none of it. A second instance of the hw5 case, added with the hybrid-retrieval measurement so the answer-key failure is watched twice.

questions.question: What is the sifting property of the Dirac delta function?
What happens to the delta function when its argument is scaled, as in delta(at)?
Why is a complex exponential an eigenfunction of an LTI system?
What signal has the Gaussian spectrum X(jw) = e^{-w^2}?
How are the Fourier series coefficients of a periodic impulse train found by the direct method?
questions.note: The derivation runs across seven slides, so the range is the run rather than the one slide that carries the substitution. The scanned appendix states the same pair as a single table entry, which is the trap.

questions.question: Which resistor and capacitor do I build the low-pass filter with?
questions.note: Lab 2 is the same handout for a high-pass filter and lists a 10 nF capacitor too.

questions.question: Which two component pairs do I compute the cutoff frequency for in the high-pass filter lab?
What carrier frequency should the LC tank be tuned to in the AM modulator lab?
Which diodes come in the lab kit, and how many of each?
What variable names should I use for the corner frequencies in the MATLAB Bode plot script?
How many minutes do I get for the final exam?
questions.note: The midterm and its solution both state 80 minutes in the same sentence shape.

questions.question: How do I find the impulse response of the system y(t) = integral to t-2 of x(tau) e^{-2(t-tau)} dtau?
questions.note: The practice midterm poses this system verbatim and works none of it out.

questions.question: What are the four Fourier representations for continuous and discrete, periodic and non-periodic signals?
How is the DTFT of a periodic sequence related to its DTFS coefficients?
What does the second law of thermodynamics say about entropy?
How do I rebase a branch onto main and resolve the conflicts?
